highlightAliases.old: Neurovascular Assessment Examination of the vascular system, including auscultation for cranial and carotid bruits, palpation of peripheral pulses, and assessment of blood pressure (lying, sitting, and standing), complements the neurologic examination and should be performed on every patient.
highlightAliases.new: Examination of the vascular system, including auscultation for cranial and carotid bruits, palpation of peripheral pulses, and assessment of blood pressure (lying, sitting, and standing), complements the neurologic examination and should be performed on every patient.

highlightAliases.old: Higher Cortical Function Cortical sensory modalities, including two-point discrimination, graphesthesia, and stereognosis should be assessed.
highlightAliases.new: Cortical sensory modalities, including two-point discrimination, graphesthesia, and stereognosis should be assessed.

highlightAliases.old: Observational Assessment Observation of a patient’s level of arousal or alertness, appearance, emotion, behavior, movements, and speech provides insight into their mental status.
highlightAliases.new: Observation of a patient’s level of arousal or alertness, appearance, emotion, behavior, movements, and speech provides insight into their mental status.

highlightAliases.old: In the digit span forward test, the patient is asked to repeat increasingly long series of numbers (eg, 1, 3-7, 4-6-3, 5-19-2, etc).
highlightAliases.new: In the digit span forward test, the patient is asked to repeat increasingly long series of numbers (eg, 1, 3-7, 4-6-3, 5-1-9-2, etc).

highlightAliases.old: Gait and Station Gate and posture depend on motor, sensory, and cerebellar function.
highlightAliases.new: Gate and posture depend on motor, sensory, and cerebellar function.

highlightAliases.old: Sensory Examination Primary modalities, including light touch and temperature are tested to assess sensory function.
highlightAliases.new: Primary modalities, including light touch and temperature are tested to assess sensory function.

highlightAliases.old: Motor System Examination Muscle bulk, strength, tone, and coordination are assessed as part of the motor system examination.
highlightAliases.new: Muscle bulk, strength, tone, and coordination are assessed as part of the motor system examination.

highlightAliases.old: Cognitive Assessment The assessment of cognitive function should be conducted methodically and should assess comprehensively the major domains of neuropsychological function (attention, memory, language, visuospatial skills, executive ability).
highlightAliases.new: The assessment of cognitive function should be conducted methodically and should assess comprehensively the major domains of neuropsychological function (attention, memory, language, visuospatial skills, executive ability).

highlightAliases.old: Pathologic and Primitive Reflexes The Babinski sign is dorsiflexion of the great toe with plantar stimulation.
highlightAliases.new: The Babinski sign is dorsiflexion of the great toe with plantar stimulation.

highlightAliases.old: Cerebellar Examination Cerebellar function and coordination may be disrupted by many types of motor and sensory abnormalities.
highlightAliases.new: Cerebellar function and coordination may be disrupted by many types of motor and sensory abnormalities.

highlightAliases.old: Neuropsychiatric Assessment The neuropsychiatric interview of the patient includes the evaluation of thought form, thought content, and insight.
highlightAliases.new: The neuropsychiatric interview of the patient includes the evaluation of thought form, thought content, and insight.
